adds.rationale: Microsoft's Feb-19 Majorana 1 topological-qubit chip reveal reignited the quantum wave after a rough January, and a diversified ETF captures the buildup without single-name blowup risk given how volatile the pure-plays were this quarter.

news_evidence.summary: Microsoft unveils Majorana 1, its first quantum processor built on topological qubits, claiming a path to a million-qubit chip
Quantum computing stocks (IonQ +2.1%, Rigetti +6.9%, D-Wave +11.1%) rally after Microsoft's chip reveal

removes.rationale: DeepSeek's Jan-27 shock erased a record $589B of Nvidia market cap in a single session and put the first real crack in the AI-capex-efficiency consensus, a peak-enthusiasm signal for a wave the profile explicitly says to trim before it crests, and AI was the most concentrated bucket on the watchlist (2 of 5 slots) heading into this call.

news_evidence.summary: Nvidia shares tumble 17%, wiping out $589 billion in market cap, the largest single-day loss in US stock-market history, as China's DeepSeek claims comparable AI performance at a fraction of the cost

rationale_overall: This swap de-risks the watchlist's AI overweight (down from 2 of 5 slots to 1, keeping MSFT for its own quantum optionality and cloud diversification) and rotates the freed slot into quantum computing, the profile's #3-ranked next wave, right as Microsoft's Majorana 1 announcement pulled the sector out of a rough January and back into a visible buildup phase; a diversified ETF (QTUM, launched 2018) is the prudent vehicle given how sharply the single-name quantum stocks whipsawed. Post-swap the watchlist holds one ticker per wave across AI (MSFT), rockets (RKLB), nuclear (OKLO), robotics (BOTZ), and quantum (QTUM) — materially better thematic spread. Defense stayed on the sidelines despite real Q1 evidence because the cap only supported one clean swap and none of MSFT/RKLB/OKLO/BOTZ showed a guardrail-qualifying breach to fund a second one; defense is the top watch item for the next rebalance.
